To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the long propriospinal neurone population is composed of three types, each of which receives a specific pattern of inputs, and each type of long propriospinal neurons is functionally specialized for different motor tasks.
there exist three types of long propriospinal neurone (PN) with different input and that the PNs of different types are differentially activated during forelimb movements.
the long propriospinal neurone system is organized in such a way that it can contribute to the adjustment and modulation of hindlimb postural activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the organization of the spinal cord in terms of the functions of the different subpopulations of spinal neurones.
the analysis of the spinal mechanisms of the postural control of the hindlimb.
the analysis of the functional organization of spinal neurones which contribute to the control of posture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the long C5-C3 PNs are a heterogeneous population of neurones, which are excited from the pyramidal tract, the medial and the lateral vestibular nuclei and the reticular formation, and which project to the lumbar segments of the spinal cord where they modulate the basic hindlimb posture.
the long C2-C5 PNs are a heterogeneous population of neurones, some of them being involved in the control of hindlimb motoneurones and some of them being interneurones.
long C3-C6 PNs are part of the spinal cord circuitry for the control of hindlimb muscles during forelimb movements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the long C4-C5 propriospinals are a heterogeneous population with a complex pattern of synaptic inputs from pyramidal and other descending systems as well as from the vestibular system.
the long C4-C5 PNs are involved in the control of hindlimb movements during forelimb movement.
the long C5-C6 PNs are a part of the spinal circuitry for the control of hindlimb movements and that they are modulated by the vestibular, rubrospinal, reticulospin and pyramidal systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the long C2-C5 propriospinals (PNs) have been shown to have three distinct functional classes.
the spinal cord is not a passive structure but is an important component in motor control.
the long C5-C7 propriospinal neurone population is not homogeneous, and that it is composed of at least three different subpopulations of cells.
